meta.title: Swordland showdown — Kingshot 777
meta.description: Member guide to Kingshot Swordland Showdown: what actually scores, the map, the 15-minute unlock, your role on the field, squad setup, healing and how to stay alive.

tldr.heading: TL;DR
items: Bi-weekly, the battle is always Sunday and lasts exactly one hour. Two alliances field a Legion of up to 30 combatants plus 10 substitutes.
Troops are only injured, never lost. Everything heals for free when you leave the battlefield. Play aggressively.

Two separate reward tracks. Alliance rewards follow Legion 1's win or loss; your personal rewards follow your own Personal Relic Point rank. A top scorer on the losing side out-earns a passenger on the winning side.
Clear your infirmary before it starts. You cannot enter with injured troops waiting.
Nobody scores in the spawn zone. Points come from moving.

before.heading: Before you enter
items: Clear the infirmary. This is a hard requirement — injured troops waiting to heal block entry entirely.
If you registered, show up. A no-show still counted toward your side's power rating but contributes nothing.
Substitutes only auto-fill in the first 3 minutes (180 seconds), first-come-first-served. If you're a sub, be at the gate from the whistle.
Heal up and recall your marches beforehand. Enter at full strength.

firstControlBonus.heading: First control bonus
firstControlBonus.body: The first alliance to fully occupy a building after its capture timer completes gets a large one-off Alliance and Personal bonus. First capture of the Swordshrine alone is 9,000 Alliance / 4,500 Personal Relic Points, and taking first control of every Phase 1 building totals 26,400 Relic Points. This is why spreading out at the start beats stacking one target.

occupation.heading: Ongoing occupation
occupation.holdBonus: 30-minute hold bonus: once your alliance has held a building for 30 straight minutes, it starts paying Personal Relic Points at a higher rate — the patch notes don't say how much. A building nearing that threshold is worth more than its base rate suggests, both to hold and to steal.

bankedPoints.heading: Banked points and Baggage Trains
bankedPoints.body: 50% of a building's accumulated alliance points sit visibly above it. Lose the building and those points drop on the ground as Baggage Trains that either side can pick up with a march, and they count for both Alliance and Personal points. Looting is not passive — send a march the moment a building flips, yours or theirs.

defeatingTroops.heading: Defeating troops

headers.personalPointsPerPower: Personal points per 10,000 enemy soldier power defeated

defeatingTroops.body: Kills pay Personal points only — no Alliance points at all. Offense pays roughly double defense, and in a high-power kingdom you can hit the personal cap within minutes purely from combat.

undercellars.heading: Undercellars
undercellars.body: Unmarked gathering nodes that spawn around the Swordshrine. Find them with the magnifying glass on the minimap and send a march like you would to a resource node. Slower than buildings but usually uncontested, so they're reliable, safe income for lower-power players. Late in the battle they can be worth 20–40k points in total — don't sleep on them.

rows.whatItDoes: Centre of the map, opens at 15 min.
rows.whyYouCare: Highest point flow on the field. The main prize — but not mandatory to win.

rows.whatItDoes: Flank the shrine, open from the start.
rows.whyYouCare: The real point engine. Hold at least one all match.
Steady income and cheap first-control bonuses.

rows.whatItDoes: Buff: halves the free Advanced Teleporter cooldown for the whole alliance.
rows.whyYouCare: First pick in Phase 1. Mobility wins the map.
Highest-priority buff in Phase 1, since every first-control bonus is large.

rows.whatItDoes: Buff: +15% attack and 15% damage reduction for your alliance. Opens at 15 min.
rows.whyYouCare: Take it the moment it opens — it applies to every fight afterwards.

rows.whatItDoes: Opens at 15 min. Sends mercenaries at an enemy-held building.
rows.whyYouCare: No personal combat points from its kills. Use it to soften a target right before your rally, never standalone.

rows.whatItDoes: Unmarked nodes that spawn in waves near the shrine.
rows.whyYouCare: Uncontested points for anyone who can't win fights.

rows.whatMatters:
2 Sanctums, 4 Abbeys, Bell Tower and Royal Stables are live.
Priority: Royal Stables → Bell Tower → a Sanctum → Abbeys.
Spread out to claim as many first-control bonuses as possible.
Strongest players can pressure enemy cities at the same time to pull defenders out of buildings.

Swordshrine, Hall of Reformation and Mercenary Camp unlock.
Take Reformation immediately; the buff applies to every fight afterwards.
Tunnelling everything into the Swordshrine while giving up Sanctums and Abbeys is a losing play.
If the shrine is too contested, pivot to holding both Sanctums plus Bell Tower, Reformation and the Abbeys.

Undercellar waves spawn at 15 min and 20 min.
The last 5–10 minutes are the comeback window.
Enemy buildings with big banked reserves are the highest-value targets, because flipping them dumps a huge Baggage Train cluster.

items.heading: Attacker
items.body: Teleport onto contested or weakly-held buildings, open rallies, burn enemy cities to force players to teleport out of their garrisons, then move on. Golden rule: attackers capture and move on, they do not sit in garrisons.

items.heading: Defender / joiner
items.body: Garrison the buildings you're assigned, keep your top 3 heroes home enough to survive, fill garrison slots so the enemy can't solo the building, and reinforce neighbours. If a stronger player reinforces you and you then teleport away, his garrisoned troops stay with you.

items.heading: Gatherer / support
items.body: Chase Baggage Trains the instant a building flips, gather Undercellars, and join rallies as a secondary march. You can launch marches from inside the safe zone without exposing your city — this is the free-to-play scoring lane, and it works.

squadSetup.heading: Squad setup
items: Troop ratio: 50/20/30 infantry/cavalry/archers most of the time. Use 60/40/0 with Alcar, Margot or Saul, whose skills lean cavalry and infantry.

Offense and defense are the same. Kills are calculated simultaneously at the end of each mini-round, so neither side needs to "tank more". The only real difference is which scenario triggers a hero's widget, which is why the best offensive and defensive heroes are simply the latest generation with a matching widget type. Defense does not need more infantry and does not need dedicated "defensive" joiners.
For solo attacks, use the highest-generation heroes you have that are decently invested.

pvpJoinerHeroes.heading: PvP joiner heroes
pvpJoinerHeroes.intro: The same picks in both offense and defense:

healingAndMobility.heading: Healing and mobility
items: No batch healing during the event — healing speed-ups only, and the event drips out free 1h healing speed-ups slowly.

Exit to heal. Tap the scoreboard at the top and choose Leave battlefield to instantly and freely heal everything. You then wait 12 minutes before you can re-enter. With hundreds of thousands injured, that round trip beats fighting at half strength.
Don't waste healing speed-ups near the end. Troops cannot die, the infirmary cannot fill up during the event, and everything heals when the event ends.

Free march speed-ups: a permanent event-only +25% march speed charge accumulates one per minute, capped at 10 (some sources say you start with 5 and can bank up to 30). Either way, hoarding them is a mistake — spend them.

Free Advanced Teleporter roughly every 10–12 minutes, halved if your alliance holds the Royal Stables. Teleporting again before the free one recharges costs Advanced Teleporters at an escalating price (+1 each time), so one paid hop between free ones is fine; chaining several is not.

stayingAlive.heading: Staying alive
items: If a much stronger player attacks you, avoid the injuries. Deploy troops onto empty ground next to your city, teleport away, or recall your top 3 heroes if that's enough to hold.
The guard station takes heavily increased damage here. If you don't spend gems to put the fire out, 10–20 seconds is enough to force-teleport your city home.
Ask a stronger player for reinforcements. Their garrisoned troops stay with you even if you teleport.
Buy the 2h counter-recon (about 400 gems) so you can't be scouted, and use every attack and defense buff you have — a 10% or 20% gem buff multiplies rather than adds.
Scout a lot before attacking, and use 1-minute rallies liberally.

You don't have to sit next to a building. Parking in the open next to an objective makes you an easy target. Sit in the safe zone or in dead space between buildings and lean on the free march speed-ups.
A lost attack is still a win if you injured more than ~80,000 troops. Each follow-up attack gets easier. Same when defending: under 80k injured is a good trade.
Don't spam every march at one target unless they're already below ~100,000 troops. Only your main march does real damage; the rest just suicide.
Don't send your main march far away unless a strong second march or a friend is covering your city.

commonMistakes.heading: Common mistakes
items: Sitting in the spawn zone doing nothing. You score zero.
Hoarding teleporters and march speed-ups until the event ends.
Chasing only the Swordshrine and losing the Sanctums and Abbeys that actually pay.
Ignoring Undercellars and Baggage Trains. Free points nobody contests.
Attackers parking in a garrison instead of moving to the next target.
Entering with a full infirmary, or forgetting to show up after registering.
Burning healing speed-ups in the last minutes, when everything heals for free at the end anyway.
